news.headline: ADAR1 Capital Management Continues Building Stake in Tenax Therapeutics, Crosses 13% Ownership
news.summary: ADAR1 Capital Management has kept adding TENX shares in open-market purchases through early September 2026, building on its late-August accumulation (4.85M shares, ~13% stake, at ~$1.77) with further buys around $1.79-$1.85. The sustained institutional buying at depressed post-crash prices sparked premarket rallies and fueled a deep-value debate around the stock.

news.headline: Tenax Therapeutics Presents Full Phase 3 LEVEL Data in Late-Breaking Session at ESC Congress 2026
news.summary: Prof. Sanjiv Shah presented the complete LEVEL dataset in Munich, confirming that TNX-103's treatment effect concentrates in patients with baseline 6MWD below the trial median of 333 meters, who saw a 26.3-meter benefit (p=0.0112) and a 47% NT-proBNP reduction versus placebo. The data reinforced Tenax's rationale for pursuing an enriched-population registrational strategy with the FDA.

news.headline: Tenax Therapeutics (NASDAQ:TENX) Rating Lowered to Strong Sell at Wall Street Zen
news.summary: Wall Street Zen cut its rating on Tenax from Sell to Strong Sell days after the failed Phase 3 LEVEL readout. The downgrade reflects post-trial-failure caution even as some sell-side peers stayed constructive.

news.headline: Piper Sandler Maintains Tenax Therapeutics With Buy Rating, Cuts Target Price to $14
news.summary: Piper Sandler kept its Buy rating but slashed its price target sharply following the LEVEL trial's missed primary endpoint. The firm still sees value in the subgroup and biomarker data despite the setback.

news.headline: TENX Downgraded by Evercore ISI Group -- Price Target Lowered to $5.00
news.summary: Evercore ISI cut Tenax to In Line from Outperform and slashed its target from $39 to $5, one of several sharp analyst downgrades after the Phase 3 miss. William Blair and Guggenheim also downgraded the stock around the same time.

news.headline: Tenax Therapeutics Announces Topline Results from Phase 3 LEVEL Clinical Trial of TNX-103 in Patients with PH-HFpEF
news.summary: The pivotal LEVEL trial missed its primary endpoint (6-minute walk distance, +3.5m vs placebo, p=0.63) and its key secondary endpoint (KCCQ), though prespecified subgroups of sicker patients showed a 26.3-meter benefit, a 49% NT-proBNP reduction, and a 3.5 mmHg RVSP improvement. Shares collapsed roughly 87-90% on the news, and Tenax said it will seek an FDA Type C meeting to discuss a revised registrational path.

catalysts.label: FDA Type C meeting on levosimendan path forward
catalysts.detail: Tenax has requested a Type C meeting with the FDA (with parallel EMA scientific consultation) to present the full LEVEL dataset, now reinforced by the ESC Congress presentation, and discuss an enriched-population registrational strategy focused on patients with lower baseline walk distance. The FDA's prior agreement that a single Phase 3 trial at p=0.01 could support an NDA is expected to be a key discussion point. The meeting had not yet occurred as of early September 2026.

catalysts.label: LEVEL-2 Phase 3 enrollment completion
catalysts.detail: The global, ~540-patient LEVEL-2 registrational trial (2:1 randomization) remains ongoing, with enrollment completion previously guided to end of 2027. Design and enrollment criteria may still be revised pending FDA feedback from the pending Type C meeting, potentially narrowing the study toward the enriched, lower-baseline-6MWD population.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings / cash runway and strategy update
catalysts.detail: Next quarterly report should update the cash position (runway guided to Q2 2028 as of Q2 2026) and provide concrete next steps for the levosimendan program following the LEVEL trial failure and the FDA Type C meeting.

pulse: TENX shares have stabilized in the $1.80-$1.90 range (market cap roughly $70-110M depending on share count used) after the catastrophic 87-90% collapse following the August 10, 2026 Phase 3 LEVEL primary-endpoint miss, with the full dataset presented at ESC Congress on August 29 reinforcing a narrower enriched-population rationale (26.3m walk-distance benefit and 47-49% NT-proBNP reduction in sicker, lower-baseline patients). The most notable recent development is sustained aggressive open-market buying by ADAR1 Capital Management, which has built a stake above 13% since late August at prices near the post-crash lows, signaling a deep-value bet even as sell-side analysts remain split (some slashed targets to $5 while keeping Buy ratings, others moved to Strong Sell). Watch for the still-pending FDA Type C meeting outcome, which will determine whether Tenax can pursue a narrower, faster registrational path or must redesign LEVEL-2, alongside the Q3 2026 earnings update on cash runway.
